title: HarmonICA: Quasi-Time-Invariant ICA for Motor Unit Decomposition during Dynamic Contractions
abstract: arXiv:2406.19581v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Decomposing surface electromyography (EMG) into the spike trains of individual motor neurons is a long-standing inverse problem and a key step toward motor-neuron-driven neural interfaces such as prosthetics and exoskeletons. The standard approach, independent component analysis (ICA) of the multichannel signal, assumes that the mixing from neurons to electrodes is stationary in time. This assumption fails during movement, when volume-conductor deformation makes the mixing time-varying, and current decomposition algorithms are correspondingly restricted to isometric contractions. We introduce HarmonICA, a quasi-time-invariant ICA formulation in which a static linear separator is preceded by a learned, low-rank, time-varying invertible transformation. The separator is trained with an independence loss on the uncompensated projection, and the transformation with a stationarity loss on the recovered source. Gradients are not share

translated_title: HarmonICA：用于动态收缩期间运动单元分解的准时不变独立成分分析
translated_abstract: 将表面肌电信号（EMG）分解为单个运动神经元的脉冲序列是一个长期存在的逆问题，也是实现运动神经元驱动的神经接口（如假肢和外骨骼）的关键步骤。标准方法是对多通道信号进行独立成分分析（ICA），其假设从神经元到电极的混合过程在时间上是平稳的。这一假设在运动过程中会失效，因为体积导体的形变使得混合过程随时间变化，因此现有的分解算法只能局限于等长收缩。我们提出了HarmonICA，这是一种准时不变的ICA形式，其中在静态线性分离器之前加入了一个可学习的、低秩的、时变的可逆变换。分离器通过对未补偿投影施加独立性损失进行训练，而变换则通过对恢复出的源信号施加平稳性损失进行训练。梯度不共享……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了HarmonICA方法，通过在静态线性分离器前引入可学习的低秩时变可逆变换，克服混合过程时变的限制，首次将独立成分分析推广到动态收缩条件下的表面肌电运动单元分解。
en_tdlr: HarmonICA extends ICA-based motor unit decomposition to dynamic contractions by prepending a learned low-rank time-varying invertible transformation to a static linear separator, overcoming the failure of the stationary mixing assumption.
